key_takeaways: git log variations (--oneline, --graph, --all) enable efficient repository history navigation
Commit hashes (SHA-1) provide immutable, content-based identifiers that work across distributed repositories
git diff shows changes between states: working vs staging (git diff), staging vs repository (git diff --staged), working vs repository (git diff HEAD)
git show provides detailed inspection of specific commits including full diff of changes
.gitignore prevents tracking files that shouldn't be versioned: dependencies, secrets, build artifacts, OS files
Professional commit messages follow format: <type>(<scope>): <subject> with optional body explaining what and why
Atomic commits contain one logical change each, enabling surgical reverts and maintainable history
Reviewing changes with git diff --staged before committing prevents security issues (API keys) and quality problems (debug statements, unintended changes)
Dependency manifest files (package.json, requirements.txt) are the documentation—commit these, not node_modules/ or venv/
Compiled/generated files (.pyc, *.class, *.o) are machine-specific and should be excluded via .gitignore
